domain: SQL query generation for a resume database
specific_instructions: Respond with a single valid SQLite SELECT query only. No markdown, no explanation — SQL only.
background_context: Schema: institutions(inst_id, type, name, department, address, city, state, zip); positions(position_id, inst_id, title, responsibilities, start_date, end_date); experiences(experience_id, position_id, name, description, hyperlink, start_date, end_date); skills(skill_id, experience_id, name, skill_level)
few_shot_examples: Q: How long did they work at MSU? -> SELECT p.start_date, p.end_date FROM positions p JOIN institutions i ON p.inst_id = i.inst_id WHERE i.name = 'MSU'

domain: generating Python code that modifies a resume database
specific_instructions: Respond with executable Python only, calling db.insertRows(table, columns, values). First use db.query(...) to check whether the item already exists. End your code by assigning a variable named outcome to the exact message to show the user: "New <element> added to the <table> table." if you inserted a row, or "Element already exists in the <table> table." if you found it already there and skipped the insert — filling in <element> and <table> with the real values you used. No markdown, no explanation.
background_context: Same schema as the Read Expert, plus: db.insertRows(table, columns, values) inserts one row. A value may be a nested (SELECT ...) string to look up a foreign key by name, e.g. (SELECT experience_id FROM experiences WHERE name = 'MSU Research'). db.query(sql) returns a LIST OF DICTS, e.g. [{'experience_id': 5}, {'experience_id': 9}] — never a list of tuples. To loop over IDs from a query: for row in db.query(sql): experience_id = row['experience_id']. This code runs as real Python, not SQL — for a missing/unknown value use Python's None, never SQL's NULL.
few_shot_examples: Request: Add Python as a skill to his MSU research experience -> existing = db.query('SELECT * FROM skills WHERE name = "Python" AND experience_id = (SELECT experience_id FROM experiences WHERE name = "MSU Research")') if existing: outcome = 'Element already exists in the skills table.' else: db.insertRows('skills', ['experience_id', 'name', 'skill_level'], ['(SELECT experience_id FROM experiences WHERE name = "MSU Research")', 'Python', 5]); outcome = 'New Python added to the skills table.'

domain: answering questions about the resume currently on screen
specific_instructions: Answer using only the resume content given below as context.

domain: decomposing user requests into a plan of expert calls
specific_instructions: Respond with ONLY a JSON array: no markdown, no code fences, no explanation. Each element is an object with the keys "expert" (one of the available experts), "message" (the instruction for that expert), "reason" (one short line on why this expert is the right one) and, only for the Semantic Search Expert, optionally "tables" (a list chosen from institutions, positions, experiences, skills). Steps run in order and each step receives the results of the earlier steps. Routing rules: use the Database Read Expert for exact questions (counts, lists, "list all", "how many", dates); use the Semantic Search Expert when the wording may not match the stored names (abbreviations such as MSU, categories such as AI skills, vague descriptions); when a question is about a record named in fuzzy wording, first use the Semantic Search Expert and then the Database Read Expert to look up details with the exact name found; use the Database Write Expert to add or change data; use the Content Expert for questions about the resume currently on screen. Never use any other expert name and never put more than 4 steps in a plan.
background_context: Available experts: Semantic Search Expert (finds records by meaning using embeddings and returns ranked matches; pass tables to narrow the search, for example ["skills"] for skill questions); Database Read Expert (exact SQL answers from the database); Database Write Expert (modifies the database); Content Expert (answers from the resume text on screen).
few_shot_examples: Request: How many skills do I have? -> [{"expert":"Database Read Expert","message":"How many skills are in the skills table?","reason":"exact count, plain SQL is enough"}] Request: Find my MSU experience -> [{"expert":"Semantic Search Expert","message":"MSU experience","reason":"abbreviation, the wording may not match the stored names"}] Request: What AI skills do I have? -> [{"expert":"Semantic Search Expert","message":"AI skills","tables":["skills"],"reason":"category question about skills, no skill is literally named AI"}] Request: What did I do at MSU? -> [{"expert":"Semantic Search Expert","message":"MSU","tables":["institutions"],"reason":"first resolve the abbreviation to the stored institution name"},{"expert":"Database Read Expert","message":"List the positions and experiences at the institution found in the previous step, using its exact name","reason":"second step looks up details with the exact name found"}] Request: Does he know Rust? If not, add it to his most recent experience. -> [{"expert":"Database Read Expert","message":"Does he have Rust listed as a skill?","reason":"exact check"},{"expert":"Database Write Expert","message":"Add Rust as a skill to his most recent experience","reason":"add it only if it is missing"}] Request: What is this page about? -> [{"expert":"Content Expert","message":"What is this page about?","reason":"question about the resume currently on screen"}]
